newsitem.title: USA: Lonely at top, dlr/mark may seek much lower ground.
newsitem.headline: Lonely at top, dlr/mark may seek much lower ground.

text.p: The dollar, after a brief solo ascent to fresh highs against the mark on Friday, now seems to suffer from a bout of technical acrophobia without similar gains versus the Swiss franc and the yen to coax it higher.
Analysts said the dollar has been in a topping process against the mark since March and the apogee may have been reached when it briefly scaled 1.74 marks.

The greenback's advance to a 39-month high at 1.7423 marks on Friday was not confirmed by new highs against any other currency -- denoting a sharp deviation from the pattern of broad-based dollar gains seen earlier this year, experts said.

"The big difference between this new high in dollar/mark and the series of new highs it had previously is that the dollar had confirmed its top against other currencies, i.e. the yen and Swiss franc," said Darren Spain, a global foreign exchange analyst at Credit Suisse First Boston.
The dollar made a series of new highs against the mark in 1997, reaching 1.7210 on March 7, 1.7375 on April 15 and 1.7389 on April 28.

Dollar/yen, however, is in a broad consolidation, unable to muster much strength since tumbling more than 12 percent from a 56-month high at 127.47 on May 1 to 111.98 on May 20. It stood around 114.50 early Friday afternoon.
By the same token, dollar/Swiss is also mired well below its 1997 peak, dragging its heels in a series of lower highs since it topped at 1.4922 on March 6, its strongest since late 1993.

"Historically, when dollar/mark makes new highs that are not confirmed by dollar/Swiss, that has given us some very good change-of-trend signals," said Martin Autotte, technical foreign exchange analyst at CIBC Wood Gundy, in Montreal.
By early afternoon on Friday the dollar had already backed off more than two pfennigs from its early high, which analysts described as the fourth of the series of unsustained new highs this year.

"Everytime we start to see a new high, it's met with pretty good selling interest," said David Solin, partner at Foreign Exchange analytics. "It's part of a much bigger topping process that's been kind of going on for the last couple of months."
"The risk for next week is for a move sharply lower and for this month is for a move back towards 1.66 marks," said Spain.
Autotte said dollar/mark has started a correction which will probably take us down to 1.7150 early next week.
At 1245 EDT/1600 GMT on Friday the dollar was at 1.7260/70 marks, down from 1.7375/85 at the open.
